newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish police find mortar tubes on border.
newsitem.headline: Irish police find mortar tubes on border.

text.p: Irish police said on Wednesday they found 21 tubes for launching guerrillas' mortar bombs in a search along the border with Northern Ireland.
They were unearthed in a bunker dug into the ground near Hackballscross in County Louth together with eight frames for mounting the devices.
No explosives were found in the bunker but a search was underway to see if more equipment was hidden.
It was not immediately clear which guerrilla organisation hid the equipment but the Irish Republican Army (IRA) or another group fighting to end British rule of Northern Ireland was suspected.
In June, police found a major IRA arms factory and storage bunker in Portarlington, south of Dublin, where mortar bombs were being primed for use.

Police said the find was a major blow to the guerrillas but security sources say the organisation has enough guns and explosives hidden in Ireland and elsewhere to keep fighting into the 21st century.
The IRA, which has fought British rule of Northern Ireland for 27 years, ended a ceasefire in February and went back to war against British targets in London, Manchester and Germany.
Last week British police found several tonnes of explosive and automatic weapons in a raid on houses in London and said they had foiled an imminent strike against a British target.
